description: An exemption is a named class of reason for which an analyzer keeps a symbol the reference graph alone would report. Each class has a detection rule an analyzer computes from its language's type information and program graph, never from a text search except where a class says so; the analyzer records the class name in the symbol's `retained_by` field, lists the held-back symbols and their classes on request, and lets a maintainer disable any class by name so an exemption suspected of hiding a defect can be tested. Every recorded exemption names the source site its evidence was found at and carries one clause of detail naming the relation and the thing it relates to, `satisfies io.Writer` or `named by {{.Title}}`: a class derived from a type relation names the conversion or the consumer site, a class derived from a text match names the position of the matching text, the generated-file class names the package clause of a generated Go file and the first line of a generated TypeScript file, and the assembly and plugin class names the assembly directive, or the package clause of the file that declares the symbol where the evidence is the shape of the package. An exemption's evidence site decides which run records it: under a production sweep, which counts no reference from a test file, an exemption whose evidence site is in a test file does not hold, for every class in this file. A conversion, an encoder or template destination, a directive, a generated-file clause or a matching text in a test file retains nothing for production, exactly as a reference from a test file makes nothing live for production, and it counts as a test reference to each symbol it would retain, as a reference from a test file does: the symbol is reported under the code its production and test references select, so a symbol that production code never references and that such evidence alone retains is reported as test-only use rather than under an unused code; a run that counts test references records the exemption. The vocabulary is closed: a conformance expectation whose `retained_by` names a class absent from this file is a defect in the expectation. Fields: `languages` names the languages the class runs on (`go`, `ts`); `confidence` uses the report's reachability vocabulary, `certain` for a class derived from a type relation and `possible` for a class derived from a text match; `rule` is the detection rule stated for an implementer in any language; `mechanism` restates it in each listed language's own terms; `retains` names what the class keeps. `typescript_visibility` is present on every class that runs on TypeScript and states whether the class can retain a class member declared with the `private` modifier and whether it can retain one declared with a `#private` name; a class that retains no class member states false for both. The two differ at runtime: `private` is a compile-time constraint only, so a `private` member stays reachable by its name through a string index, a decorator, a container or a serializer, while a `#private` name cannot be named from outside its class body at all. Every class that reaches members by name therefore applies to `private` and not to `#private`, and a `#private` member with no reference in its own class body is reported whatever else the program does.

exemptions.rule: A method is retained when a value of its receiver's type reaches a position typed as an interface the method helps satisfy and the interface method it implements is called. The analyzer records every site, in the target and in each loaded consumer, where a value of type T is converted or assigned to an interface type I (an explicit conversion or a satisfaction assertion, an assignment, an argument, a return value, an element stored in an I-typed container), and every instantiation whose type argument T stands for a type parameter whose constraint is I, because the generic code calls the constraint's methods on values of T. For each recorded (T, I) pair, it retains each member of T that I requires, except a method that implements a method of I the rule of DS1203 holds for and its precondition does not exempt. In Go, where I is a defined interface type declared outside the analyzed program, code outside the analysis holds the value through I and may assert another interface on it, so the pair also retains each method by which T implements an interface that the source of the package declaring I asserts, being the interface type each type assertion and each type switch case in that source names, whichever package declares it, an interface type literal included. A site retains as a use by the declaration that holds it, so a retained method is live only while that declaration is, and it falls into that declaration's dead component with it. A satisfaction assertion is a root while T is built by live code, being referenced by a declaration other than a satisfaction assertion that is live without the assertion, applied until no further declaration joins, and its pair then retains as any other does. The assertion of a type only dead code builds is no root and retains nothing: it falls with T, so the type, its methods and the assertion delete together. The assertion is not a use of I beyond itself: when nothing else uses I as a type, I is still reported as an unused satisfaction assertion, each method of I is reported under DS1203, and the methods of T that implement them fall with those findings.
exemptions.retains: For each recorded (T, I) pair, the members of T that I requires, except a method implementing a method of I that DS1203 reports, while the declaration holding the site is live. In Go, where I is declared outside the analyzed program, the methods by which T implements an interface a type assertion or a type switch case in the source of the package declaring I names, as well.

mechanism.go: Build the conversion set from the type-checked program: an assertion of the form `var _ I = (*T)(nil)` or `var _ I = T{}`, a value passed to a parameter of type I, a value returned into a result of type I, a value assigned to a variable or field of type I, an element stored into an I-typed slice, map, channel or struct field, and a type argument T of an instantiation whose type parameter's constraint is I. For each (T, I) pair, `types.Implements(T, I)` decides satisfaction, and the methods of T that I requires are retained, except a method implementing a method of I that DS1203 reports. Each is a use by the declaration that holds the site. Where I is a defined interface type of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, retain as well every method by which T, or a pointer to it, implements an interface that package's source asserts, as `types.Implements` decides: the interface type of each type assertion `x.(J)` and of each type switch case written in that package's source, whichever package declares it, an interface type literal among them. A type assertion or a case naming a type that is not an interface asserts nothing. The analysis reads that package's source for its type assertions and type switches alone, wherever in that source they stand and whatever value they assert on. A generic interface type that is not instantiated is skipped, and so is an interface that holds a type term or embeds `comparable`. An assertion of a type that no live declaration other than an assertion references is no root, retains nothing and falls with the type. A type registered with `flag.Var`, or used as an `io.Writer`, an `http.RoundTripper` or a `sort.Interface`, is an ordinary member of the conversion set, so those methods are retained here and by no other class.
mechanism.ts: Build the same conversion set over class instance types flowing into interface-typed positions: an `implements` clause, an assignment, an argument, a return value, an element stored in an interface-typed container, and a type argument whose type parameter's constraint is the interface. For each (class, interface) pair, the checker's assignability test decides satisfaction, and the members the interface requires are retained, except a method that implements a method of that interface DS1203 reports. Each is a use by the declaration that holds the site, the class itself for an `implements` clause.

exemptions.rule: A type whose values reach a consumer that inspects them by name at runtime has the members that consumer reads retained, on the type and on every type the consumer walks to through its fields, the types the program stores in an interface-typed field included. An encoder's argument that is a composite literal reaches the type of each value the literal writes into an interface-typed position, and an argument whose type is a defined interface type reaches every type the program converts to that interface. A conversion to any reaches no destination by itself. What is retained is per destination. A destination that reads fields retains the exported fields and the tagged fields, except a field an encoder skips because its tag gives it the key `-`, while a decoding destination fills fields through reflection, which is neither a read nor a write of this contract, and retains none of them, the `XMLName` field an XML decoder compares excepted. A function that only decodes into its argument is a decoding destination and reads no field, wherever it is declared, save a field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes, which the decoder reads to decode into the value the field holds. Each destination retains the methods it resolves by name and no other method, so a type only decoding destinations reach keeps the decoding methods they resolve and no other method. A consumer the analysis cannot read counts as one that reads every field and resolves by name the methods its own code can name: a value passed as an interface-typed argument to a function or method outside the analyzed program, a slice, an array or a map of such values included, has left the analysis. So has a value returned as an interface-typed result by a method that implements a method of an exported interface declared outside the analyzed program, because outside code calls that method through the interface. Code outside the analysis may read the fields of such a value and call the methods by which it satisfies an interface the callee's package declares or writes as a literal, exported or not, or an exported interface of a package in that package's import closure or of a package outside the analyzed program that imports the callee's package. A standard container stores the value and hands it back to the program unchanged, so the code of its own package is the only outside code that reads the value: such a value keeps the methods by which it satisfies an interface that package declares or writes as a literal and no field and no other method.
exemptions.retains: The exported fields and the struct fields carrying a tag on every type that flows into a destination that reads fields and on every defined type reached from those types' fields through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, or an interface-typed field, element or value through the types the program stores there, and on the types an argument's own composite literals write into its interface-typed positions and, for an argument of a defined interface type, every type the program converts to that interface, except that a standard encoder does not read a field its tag gives the key `-`. The encoding and decoding methods a standard encoder or decoder resolves by name, in the direction it runs, and no other method of a type only decoders reach. The `XMLName` field, for an XML decoder. A field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes, for a decoder. The `LogValue` method for a `log/slog` destination. The exported methods for a template engine and for a method-reaching reflection call. For a destination outside the analyzed program, the fields, the encoding and decoding methods of both directions, and every method by which the type satisfies an interface the callee's package declares or writes as a literal, or an exported interface that a package in its import closure or a package outside the analyzed program that imports it declares, or every exported method where the callee's package's imports reach a template engine. For a standard container, the methods by which the type satisfies an interface its own package declares or writes as a literal, and no field.

mechanism.go: A type T flows into the class when a value of T, or a pointer to one, reaches one of the destinations below. Retain on T the members that destination retains, and retain the same members on every defined type reached from the fields of a retained type through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, or an embedded field, applied until no further type joins. A field, an element or a map value of an interface type reaches the types of the values the program stores in it: a value converted to that interface type where it is the field's value in a composite literal, the right side of an assignment to the field, an element of a composite literal of the slice, array or map type, an argument of `append` onto it, or the right side of an assignment to an index of it. Where the stored value is an interface-typed parameter of the enclosing function, it stands for every argument a call of that function passes for that parameter, applied until no further argument joins, and a parameter no call of the program passes adds no type. The argument of a destination reaches more types of its own. Where the argument expression, read through parentheses, conversions and the address operator, is a composite literal, it reaches the type of each value the literal writes into an interface-typed position, a map key or value, a slice or array element or a struct field, keyed or positional, and so on through each composite literal it nests, whatever type the literal has. Where the argument's static type is a defined interface type, it reaches every type the program converts to that interface type, at the sites `interface-satisfaction` records. The same holds for each argument a call passes for an interface-typed parameter of a function of the program that is itself a destination. A conversion to `any`, or to an interface type literal, adds no type to an argument. The encoding entry points, being the functions and methods of `encoding/json`, `encoding/json/v2`, `encoding/xml` and `encoding/gob` whose names start with `Marshal` or `Encode`, read fields: retain each walked type's exported fields and tagged fields, except a field whose tag for that encoder, `json` for `encoding/json` and `encoding/json/v2` and `xml` for `encoding/xml`, is exactly `-`, which the encoder skips, while a tag of `-,` names the key `-` and is read. Retain as well the methods the encoder resolves by name, being `MarshalJSON`, `MarshalJSONTo`, `MarshalText` and `AppendText` for JSON, `MarshalXML`, `MarshalXMLAttr` and `MarshalText` for XML, and `GobEncode` and `MarshalBinary` for gob. The decoding entry points, whose names start with `Unmarshal` or `Decode`, fill fields through reflection, which is neither a read nor a write of this contract, so they retain no field. They retain the methods the decoder resolves by name, being `UnmarshalJSON`, `UnmarshalJSONFrom` and `UnmarshalText` for JSON, `UnmarshalXML`, `UnmarshalXMLAttr` and `UnmarshalText` for XML, and `GobDecode` and `UnmarshalBinary` for gob. A decoding entry point of `encoding/xml` also retains a field named `XMLName` of type `xml.Name`, which the decoder compares with the element's name. A decoding entry point reads a field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes anywhere, because the decoder decodes through the value the field holds, and that field is then no write-only field. An embedded field is a field to this rule, so a decoding entry point keeps it live only as it keeps any field, and it is otherwise live while a selector the program writes promotes one of its members. A field only a decoder fills and nothing reads is therefore reported, and a type only decoding entry points reach keeps the methods they resolve and no other method, whatever interfaces it satisfies. A function or method only decodes into one of its parameters when its body uses that parameter at least once, and only as an argument, unchanged or converted to an interface type, of a decoding entry point or of a function that only decodes into that argument, applied until no further function joins. A function with no body, or whose body never uses the parameter, does not. It is a decoding entry point for that parameter wherever it is declared. For a function outside the analyzed program, the analysis reads the body from the source the build list holds, for this rule alone. In a program that calls `(*json.Decoder).DisallowUnknownFields`, or passes the `json.RejectUnknownMembers` option, anywhere, a decoding entry point of `encoding/json` or `encoding/json/v2` retains the fields an encoding entry point retains as well, because the decoder then refuses a document that names a member the type lacks. Any other function or method of those four packages, a registration among them, retains what both directions retain. Fields alone are retained for a destination that reads fields and resolves no method by name: a `database/sql` `Scan` target, an argument of `reflect.DeepEqual`, and an argument of any function or method of `reflect` other than the method-reaching calls below. Fields and the `LogValue() slog.Value` method are retained for a `log/slog` destination: an argument of a `log/slog` logging function, of `slog.With`, of a `*slog.Logger` method, `With` among them, of `(*slog.Record).Add` or of an attribute constructor. A handler resolves `LogValue` by the value's own shape and not through a conversion, so no conversion exists for another class to read and this class is the only one that retains it. Fields and exported methods are retained for a destination that resolves a method by name: an argument of a function or method of `text/template` or `html/template`, and a value reaching a method-reaching `reflect` call, being `Method`, `MethodByName` or `NumMethod` on a `reflect.Value` or a `reflect.Type`, or a `reflect.Value` the program calls a method through. A destination outside the analyzed program is a value of a struct type, a pointer to one, or a slice, an array or a map whose element, key or value type is one of these, passed as an interface-typed argument to a function or method of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer and that does not only decode into that argument, recorded at the call with the detail naming the callee. So is such a value returned as an interface-typed result by a method of the analyzed program that implements a method of an exported interface declared in a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, because code outside the analysis calls the method through that interface and receives the value. It is recorded at the return statement with the detail naming the interface method, and the interface's package is the callee's package below. The walk starts at every struct type the value holds. Save for deciding whether it only decodes into that argument, the analysis reads no syntax of that function, so it is read as reading every field the class retains and as resolving by name the methods its package can name: retain the encoding and decoding methods of both directions above, and every method by which the type, or a pointer to it, implements an interface the callee's package can assert, as `types.Implements` decides: each interface type the callee's package declares, exported or not, each interface type literal written in its source, and each exported interface type declared by a package in that package's import closure or by a package outside the analyzed program that the program's import closure holds and that imports the callee's package. An unexported interface of any other package is not counted. The analysis reads the callee's package's source for its interface type literals alone. A generic interface type that is not instantiated is skipped, because `types.Implements` decides no such interface. So is an interface that holds a type term or embeds `comparable`, which only constrains a type parameter. Where the callee's package's import closure holds `text/template` or `html/template`, retain every exported method as well. Any function of the analyzed program whose interface-typed parameter it passes to such a call, or to any other destination of this class, is itself a destination that retains what its destination retains, applied until no further function joins. A standard container reaches less: an argument of a method of `sync.Map`, of a method of `Value` of `sync/atomic`, or of `context.WithValue` is stored or compared and handed back to the program unchanged, and the container's own package is the only outside code that reads it. Such a value retains every method by which the type, or a pointer to it, implements an interface type that package declares or an interface type literal its source writes, and no field and no other method. A key, and an old value a `CompareAndSwap` or `CompareAndDelete` method compares, is compared as a map key is. A conversion to `sort.Interface` is an ordinary interface conversion rather than a destination of this class, so the methods that interface requires are retained by `interface-satisfaction`.

exemptions.rule: A type whose values reach a formatting facility that calls its string or error method has that method retained, on the operand's own type and on every type the facility walks to beneath it: the facility invokes `String` or `Error` through an interface at runtime, so the method has no static reference.
exemptions.retains: The `String() string` and `Error() string` methods of the operand's type and of every defined type reached from it through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, exported or not, or an exported struct field, the exported fields of a defined struct type and of a struct type with no name included, at any depth. The reach stops at an interface-typed field.

mechanism.go: A value of type T is an operand of a function that formats its operands with the `fmt` machinery, under a verb valid for a string operand (`%v`, `%s`, `%q`, `%x`, `%X`, the wrapping verb `%w` of `fmt.Errorf`, and the verb-less print forms). Retain T's `String() string` and `Error() string` methods, and retain the same two methods on every defined type reached from T through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, exported or not, or an exported struct field, applied until no further type joins. The walk enters every type it reaches, so it walks the exported fields of a defined struct type it reaches as it walks the operand's own, and the fields of a struct type with no name as well. The walk is needed because the machinery formats an exported field at any depth and calls the field type's own `String` or `Error` method there. It stops at an interface-typed field, whose dynamic type the analysis does not see, and it does not enter an unexported field that is not embedded, which the machinery prints without calling a method on it. An embedded field is entered whether or not it is exported, because its methods are promoted to the type that embeds it and the machinery calls them through that type. The functions are the `fmt` print, format and error-construction functions (`Print`, `Println`, `Printf`, `Sprint`, `Sprintln`, `Sprintf`, `Fprint`, `Fprintln`, `Fprintf`, `Append`, `Appendln`, `Appendf`, `Errorf`), the `log` package's print, fatal and panic functions and the same methods of `*log.Logger`, the `testing.TB` methods `Log`, `Logf`, `Error`, `Errorf`, `Fatal`, `Fatalf`, `Skip` and `Skipf`, the `log/slog` logging functions and `*slog.Logger` methods (`Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`, their context forms, `Log` and `LogAttrs`), `slog.With`, `(*slog.Logger).With` and `(*slog.Record).Add`, and the `slog.Any`, `slog.Group` and `slog.Attr`-constructing functions, and any function of the analyzed program whose final parameter is variadic `...any` and which passes that parameter, or a format string together with it, to one of the functions in this list, applied until no further function joins. A format string that is not a constant binds every operand of the call. An operand of a `log/slog` logging function reaches this class and `encoding-reflection` both. A method that satisfies `io.Writer` or `http.RoundTripper` is retained by `interface-satisfaction`, not by this class.

exemptions.rule: The standard error helpers reach comparison and unwrapping methods by duck typing rather than through a declared interface, so those methods have no static reference and are retained on any type the program uses as an error.
exemptions.retains: Methods with signature `Is(error) bool`, `As(any) bool`, `Unwrap() error` or `Unwrap() []error` on a type reachable as an error.

mechanism.go: A type is reachable as an error when a value of it enters the conversion set with `error` as the interface. On such a type retain every method whose name and signature match one of the four forms `errors.Is`, `errors.As` and `errors.Unwrap` call.

exemptions.rule: A member of an enumerated type whose values can arrive by conversion rather than by name is never dead in isolation. When the type carries a string, text or binary conversion method, or a value of the type is produced from an integer or from a decoded wire value, every member of that type is retained, so that a member reached only by value is never reported.
exemptions.retains: Every member of the enumerated type.

mechanism.go: The enumerated type is a defined type whose constants are declared in an `iota` group. The class fires when the type has a `String`, `MarshalText`, `UnmarshalText`, `MarshalJSON` or `UnmarshalJSON` method, or when a value of the type is produced by a conversion from an integer type or from a decoded value (an `encoding/json` or `encoding/xml` target, a `database/sql` scan target, a `strconv` result). Retain every constant of the type.
mechanism.ts: The enumerated type is an `enum` declaration. The class fires when a value of the enum is produced by a type assertion from `number` or `string`, by the reverse mapping `E[n]`, or by a decoded value typed as `E`. Retain every member of the enum.

exemptions.rule: Every declaration in a generated file is retained by default, because the generator owns the file and a deletion there is undone at the next generation. When a project configures generated files as included, the analyzer reports findings in them instead and marks each such finding as one no mechanical edit may act on.

mechanism.go: A file is generated when it carries the standard Go generated-code header: a line matching `^// Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.$` that appears before the first non-comment, non-blank text of the file, which is the rule `go/ast.IsGenerated` implements. When generated files are configured as included, each finding in one carries `generated: true` and `fixability: none`.
mechanism.ts: A file is generated when its leading comments, the comments before its first token, hold a line of the Go header form, matching `^// Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.$`, or the documentation tag `@generated` as a word of a comment, or when it is below a directory that an applied convention row names as generated, as grammar/analysis.md states. A comment after the first token marks nothing. Retain every declaration in the file, recording the file's first line with a detail naming the header, the tag or the row. When generated files are configured as included, each finding in one carries `generated: true` and `fixability: none`.

exemptions.rule: A symbol that another compilation unit reaches by name outside the type checker's view is retained: a symbol an assembly file names, or an exported symbol of a package whose shape is a plugin's. A linker-level alias and a symbol exported to C are roots of the analysis rather than exemptions, so this class retains neither.
exemptions.retains: The symbol an assembly file names, and every exported function and variable of a plugin's main package.

mechanism.go: Retain a symbol named by a `TEXT ·name` directive in an assembly file of the same package, and an exported function or variable of a main package that declares no `main` function, which is the shape of a plugin's main package. A name a `plugin` `Lookup` call carries is retained by `reflective-lookup` in the package that holds the call.

exemptions.rule: Where the project configures template directories, or holds a component file, a member whose name appears in a template or in a component file's markup as a field or method reference is retained at the lowest confidence, and the exemption names the template site that matched. Where the language's template grammar has action delimiters, the project configures the pair the scan reads and the grammar's own pair stands where it does not. The evidence is a text match, not a type relation, so this is a weak class and it applies only where the project asked for it or holds markup no other rule reads.
exemptions.retains: The member of any kind whose name the template references, on any type, an enum member and a static member included.

mechanism.go: Scan every file under the configured template directories, parsed with the action delimiters the configuration sets in `analysis.template_delimiters` and with the `text/template` delimiters `{{` and `}}` where it sets none, and retain every exported field and method whose name appears as a field or method reference in any form the template grammar records: a field reference on the dot, on a variable, or on the result of a parenthesized pipeline or of a call, at every position of a chain, so that `.Page.Title` names `Page` and `Title`. Record the template file and line.
mechanism.ts: Scan every file under the configured template directories, and the markup of every live component file, for the member's name in an interpolation or binding position. Retain every member so named, recording the template file and line.

exemptions.rule: A symbol whose name appears as a string literal that reaches a reflective lookup call is retained at the lowest confidence, and the exemption names the lookup site. A lookup through a receiver whose type maps every string key to one value type reads that mapping rather than a member, so it retains nothing. The evidence is a string match beside a call, not a type relation, so this is a weak class.
exemptions.retains: The method, field or member whose name matches the string literal.

mechanism.go: A string literal equal to a method or field name is, or is a constant that flows into, an argument of `MethodByName` or `FieldByName` on a `reflect.Value` or `reflect.Type`, or of a `Lookup` method that resolves a name at runtime. Retain the matching method or field, recording the call site.
mechanism.ts: A string literal equal to a member name is the index of an element access (`obj["name"]`) whose receiver's type is `any` or declares no string index signature, or an argument of a `Reflect` call (`Reflect.get`, `Reflect.set`, `Reflect.has`). Retain the matching member, recording the site. An element access whose receiver's type declares a string index signature, `Record<string, unknown>` among them, reads the signature and retains nothing.

exemptions.rule: A member that carries a decorator, or whose class carries a decorator, is retained: the decorator receives the member or the class at runtime and may reach the member by name, so the decorator's own symbol counts as a reference to what it decorates.
exemptions.retains: The decorated member, and every member of a decorated class that a decorator can name at runtime.

mechanism.ts: A member is retained when a decorator expression is attached to it, or when a decorator expression is attached to its class. The retention covers `private` members, which a decorator can reach by name, and never `#private` ones.

exemptions.rule: Where the project configures a dependency-injection container, a class the container constructs has its constructor and the members the container injects retained, because the container instantiates the class and populates those members with no reference in the program's own code. A class is constructed by the container when it is registered with it or when a parameter of its constructor carries a decorator. A property or an accessor carrying a decorator does not by itself make its class one the container constructs.
exemptions.retains: The class's constructor and every injected member: each property and accessor of the class, or of a class it extends, that carries a decorator.

mechanism.ts: The class is passed to a call of a declaration `ts.injection_registrations` names, or a parameter of its constructor carries a decorator. A decorated property or accessor of a class that neither route reaches makes no class container-constructed. For a class either route reaches, retain the constructor and each property and accessor that carries a decorator, on the class and on every class it extends.

exemptions.rule: Where the project declares a framework, a member whose name matches that framework's lifecycle contract, on a class reachable as that framework's component, is retained, because the framework calls it by name.

mechanism.ts: The project declares a framework and that framework's lifecycle member names as an entry of `ts.lifecycle_contracts`. A member whose name is in that entry's list is retained when its class is reachable as a component of that framework, by registration, by a decorator or by extending a declaration the entry's `bases` names.

exemptions.rule: A value that flows into a serializer or a schema validator has its data members retained, because the serializer reads them by name at runtime: the data members of every class, interface and object type its static type names, and of every such type reached from those members' types, because the serializer walks the value it is given whatever declared the value's type. Those destinations retain one method, `toJSON`, which a serializer calls on a value that carries one, and no other. A destination outside the analyzed program retains more: a value passed to a parameter typed `unknown` or `any`, a rest parameter whose element type is one of them included, of a function the analyzed program does not declare has left the analysis, so its data members are retained together with the two conversion methods a serializer or a formatter resolves by name.
exemptions.retains: The data members of every class, interface and object type the value's static type names and of every such type reached from their members' types, being a class's properties and an interface's or an object type's property signatures. The `toJSON` member of each of those types, and the `toString` member as well for a destination outside the analyzed program. No other method or accessor.

mechanism.ts: A value is an argument of `JSON.stringify` or of a declaration `ts.serializers` names. Take the value's static type and walk it: a union or an intersection walks each constituent, an array or a tuple walks its element types, and a class, an interface or an object type literal, the object type a type alias declares included, retains its data members, being a class's properties and an interface's or an object type literal's property signatures, and its `toJSON` member, then walks each retained data member's type and each index signature's value type, applied until no further type joins. The walk stops at a type parameter, at `unknown` and at `any`, whose members the analysis does not see. Those destinations retain no other method and no accessor. A value passed to a parameter typed `unknown` or `any`, or to a rest parameter whose element type is `unknown` or `any`, such as `console.log(...data: any[])`, of a function or method none of whose declarations is in a file of the project or of a declared consumer, the compiler's library declarations included, is a destination too, recorded at the call with the detail naming the callee: retain by the same walk the same data members and each walked type's `toJSON` and `toString` members, which a serializer and a formatter resolve by the value's own shape, and no other member. A parameter typed as an interface or as an object type is not this crossing, because the callee's own declaration names the members it reads. Any function of the project whose `unknown`-typed or `any`-typed parameter, a rest parameter of either element type included, it passes to such a call, or to any other destination of this class, is itself a destination, applied until no further function joins.
